item_name: High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication — Antidepressant

lookback_source.quote: N0415C1. Antidepressant: Check if an antidepressant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

lookback_notes: 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days) for both Column 1 (N0415C1) and Column 2 (N0415C2). Per the general convention, the look-back window is the ARD plus the 6 previous calendar days (rai-manual-v1.20.1, p. 2-17: "ARD + 6 previous calendar days"). The item's own pages state the 7-day window explicitly.

coding_levels.label: Antidepressant — Indication noted

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 1 (N0415C1): Check if the resident is taking an antidepressant by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Column 2 (N0415C2): If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

source.quote: Column 2: If Column 1 is checked, check if there is an indication noted for all medications in the drug class.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

source.quote: Code all high-risk drug class medications according to their pharmacological classification, not how they are being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used (e.g., oxazepam prescribed as a hypnotic is coded as antianxiety).

source.quote: Code medications in Item N0415 according to the medication's therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification, not how it is used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Medications with more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification must be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

source.quote: Medications that have more than one therapeutic category and/or pharmacological classification should be coded in all categories/classifications assigned to the medication, regardless of how it is being used.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Combination medications are coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination; e.g., a single tablet combining an antipsychotic and an antidepressant is coded in both the antipsychotic and antidepressant categories.

source.quote: Combination medications should be coded in all categories/pharmacologic classes that constitute the combination. For example, if the resident receives a single tablet that combines an antipsychotic and an antidepressant, then both antipsychotic and antidepressant categories should be coded.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

source.quote: Include any of these medications given to the resident by any route in any setting (e.g., at the nursing home, in a hospital emergency room) while a resident of the nursing home.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

source.quote: Code a medication even if it was given only once during the look-back period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Long-acting medications given every few weeks or monthly are counted only if they are given during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Count long-acting medications, such as fluphenazine decanoate or haloperidol decanoate, that are given every few weeks or monthly only if they are given during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: For transdermal patches, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

source.quote: To code N0415, only capture the medication if the transdermal patch was applied to the resident's skin during the observation period.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Herbal and alternative medicine products are dietary supplements and should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

source.quote: Therefore, they should not be counted as medications (e.g., melatonin, chamomile, valerian root).

federal_coding_rules.rule: N0415Z1 (None of the above) is checked if none of the listed medications, including antidepressants, were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: N0415Z1. None of the above: Check if none of the medications above were taken by the resident at any time during the observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal_coding_rules.rule: Providers are responsible for coding each medication's pharmacological/therapeutic classification accurately; use of the listed external resources is not required for MDS completion.

source.quote: The above resource list is not all-inclusive, and use of these resources is not required for MDS completion.

federal_coding_rules.rule: N0415 is reached from N0300 when N0300 is coded 0 (skip pattern: If 0 → Skip to N0415, High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication).

source.quote: If 0 → Skip to N0415, High-Risk Drug Classes: Use and Indication

federal.criterion: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

source.quote: Review the resident's medical record for documentation that any of these medications were received by the resident and for the indication of their use during the 7-day lookback period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

federal.notes: Step 1 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

source.quote: Review documentation from other health care settings where the resident may have received any of these medications while a resident of the nursing home (e.g., valium given in the emergency room).

federal.notes: Step 2 of Steps for Assessment for N0415.

federal.criterion: Indication is the identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication, based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals — this documented rationale supports coding Column 2 (N0415C2).

source.quote: INDICATION The identified, documented clinical rationale for administering a medication that is based upon a physician's (or prescriber's) assessment of the resident's condition and therapeutic goals.

federal.notes: Definition box on the N0415 page.

federal.criterion: Assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the pharmacological classification on the MDS 3.0; facilities may wish to identify a consistently used resource.

source.quote: Facilities may wish to identify a resource that their staff consistently use to identify pharmacological classification as assessors should be able to identify the source(s) used to support coding the MDS 3.0.

federal.notes: Framed as a suggestion ("may wish to") but with an expectation that sources can be identified.

federal.criterion: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert for the medication's pharmacological classification, and may work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm classification.

source.quote: Assessors should consult the manufacturer's package insert, which may contain the medication's pharmacological classification. They can also work with the resident's pharmacist to confirm the medication classification(s) for a resident's medication(s).

federal.notes: Suggested resource, not a required document.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The N0415 pages do not tie this item to a payment or case-mix classification.

conflicts.topic: Wording of the Column 1 observation window for antidepressant ("7-day look-back period" vs. "7-day observation period")

positions.claim: N0415C1 uses the phrase "7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: N0415C1. Antidepressant: Check if an antidepressant medication was taken by the resident at any time during the 7-day look-back period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

positions.claim: The general N0415 coding instruction for Column 1 uses the phrase "7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days)."

source.quote: Column 1: Check if the resident is taking any medications by pharmacological classification during the 7-day observation period (or since admission/entry or reentry if less than 7 days).

conflicts.resolution: Terminology difference only; both describe the same 7-day window. No substantive conflict.
